chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ali ibn Ibrahim, both from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Abdullah ibn Yazid, both from a man from the people of Basra, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the capability (istitaah). So he said: 'Are you capable of doing what has not yet come into being?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Are you capable of stopping what has already been decreed?' He said: 'No.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'So when are you capable?' He said: 'I do not know.'

He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Indeed, God created creation and placed in them the instrument of capability, but then He did not delegate it to them. So they are capable of the deed at the time of the deed, along with the deed when they do that deed. But if they are not doing it in His dominion, they would not be capable of doing a deed they did not do — because God, Mighty and Majestic, is too Exalted for anyone to oppose Him in His dominion.'

The man of Basra said: 'So the people are compelled?' He said: 'If they were compelled, they would be excused.' He said: 'Then has He delegated to them?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then what are they?' He said: 'He foreknew from them a deed, so He placed in them the instrument of the deed — so when they do it, they are with the deed, capable.'
The man of Basra said: 'I testify that it is the Truth, and that you are the People of the House of Prophethood and the Message.'

key_terms.آلة الاستطاعة: The instrument/tool of capability — the endowment God places in creatures enabling them to act
key_terms.أهل بيت النبوة والرسالة: People of the Household of Prophethood and the Message — the Imam's family lineage from the Prophet
key_terms.الاستطاعة: Capability/Ability (istitaah) — the technical theological term for human capacity to act, central to debates on free will and compulsion
key_terms.التفويض: Delegation (tafwid) — the view that God granted humans complete independent control over their actions (rejected here)
key_terms.الجبر: Compulsion (jabr) — the view that humans are fully forced with no real choice (rejected here)
key_terms.عزّ وجل: Mighty and Majestic — honorific for God

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia teaching on human capability and free will in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the theological question of human capability (istitaah) — a central debate in early Islamic theology between compulsion (jabr) and free delegation (tafwid). In a Socratic dialogue with a man from Basra, the Imam demolishes both extremes: humans cannot act before divine will enables them (ruling out pure free will), nor are they merely compelled (which would excuse all sin). The Imam articulates the Shia doctrinal position known as 'the matter is between two matters' (al-amr bayn al-amrayn): God foreknew human choices and created the instrument of capability within them, so they are capable precisely when and as they act — not before, not independently. The Basran questioner, likely familiar with Mu'tazilite or Ash'arite positions, is so convinced that he testifies to the Imams' authority over prophetic knowledge.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya and Ali Bin Ibrahim, altogether from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam and Abdullah Bin Yazeed, altogether from a man from the people of Al Basra who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the capability. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are you capable of doing what has not come into being (started)?’ He said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are you capable of ending what has already happened (started)?’ He said, ‘No’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘So when are you capable?’ He said, ‘I don’t know’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created creatures, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Made a tool to be inside them, the tool of capability. Then He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Delegate it to them, so they are capable of the deed at the time of the deed, along with the deed when they are doing that deed. So when they are not doing it in His<sup>azwj</sup> Kingdom, they would not happen to be capable of doing a deed they did not do, because Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Mightier than that He<sup>azwj</sup> should be opposed in His<sup>azwj</sup> Kingdom by anyone’.

The man of Al-Basra said, ‘So the people are being Compelled’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If they are being Compelled, they would be excused’. He said, ‘So He<sup>azwj</sup> Delegates to them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. He said, ‘So what are they?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>azwj</sup> Knew from them the doers, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Made a tool of the deed to be in them. So when they are doing, they would be with the deed, capable’.

The man of Al-Basra said, ‘I testify that it is the Truth, and you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> (Imams<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>) are the People<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> of the Household of the Prophet-hood and the Message’.
